strengths: Clean per-resource route modularization (card/allowlist/pair/inbox/artifact/health) with dependency injection of the db and shared rate limiter (server.ts:42-49).

W11 opaque-storage constraint respected: only envelope routing fields (from/to/thread/seq/type/id) are parsed for allowlist/seq enforcement; payloads and artifact blobs are stored verbatim and never decoded (allowlist.ts:91-113, inbox.ts:121-159, artifact.ts:12-29).
All SQL uses parameterized prepared statements — no injection surface; idempotent inserts via ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING for inbox/artifact.
Core DELIVERABLE scenarios are covered by tests: non-bonded sender drop (403), 401+challenge nonce, reused-nonce 403, gap_detected 409, and per-IP rate limiting (inbox.test.ts:102-212).
Content-addressed artifact integrity: PUT verifies sha256(blob) === hash before storing (artifact.ts:15-19). Challenge TTL is exactly 60s and single-use via the `used` flag (inbox.ts:12,92-111).

issues.description: verifyChallenge returns 404 for a nonce not present in the DB, but the spec's challenge-response section states a bad/expired/reused nonce should return 403. An unknown/fabricated nonce is a 'bad' nonce and should return 403 for consistency.

GET /inbox returns only { envelopes } and never exposes a received_at cursor, so a client has no way to advance the spec'd `since=T` parameter. As a result the `since` mechanism is effectively unusable beyond since=0, and gap detection (which assumes seq starts at 1 for the returned window) only functions correctly for full since=0 pulls. Works for the §8 demo happy path but the incremental-pull path is incomplete.
In-memory rate-limit `buckets` Map is never evicted; entries accumulate one per (ip, path) indefinitely, causing slow unbounded memory growth in a long-running relay.

Expired/used challenge rows are never garbage-collected — every GET /inbox without sig inserts a new nonce row, so the challenges table grows unbounded. Same applies to pair_sessions (only cleaned lazily on GET of that specific expired session).

createRelayServer is a misleading alias that simply returns createRelayApp() without starting an HTTP listener despite its name implying a running server; index.ts exports both, which may confuse consumers.
